scope: The share of a lower-wage worker's pay each state paid family and medical leave program replaces, read from the benefit quotes in state-paid-leave-premiums-2026.json (each quote's page is that file's benefit.sourceUrl). A part-time town worker's weekly wage sits in each program's first tier, so the first-tier rate is the one recorded.

US-CA.reading: The quote gives 70% to 90% depending on income; lower incomes receive the higher share.

US-CO.reading: The first $804.46 of weekly wages is replaced at 90%.

US-CT.reading: Weekly wages at or below 40 times the state minimum wage are replaced at 95%.

US-DC.reading: The sliding scale replaces up to 90%, the top of the scale going to lower wages.

US-MA.reading: Wages up to half the state average weekly wage are replaced at 80%.

US-MD.reading: Not read: the pages give only the weekly maximum.

US-ME.reading: Tier 1 replaces 90% of wages up to half the state average weekly wage.

US-MN.reading: 55% to 90%; the 90% goes to the lowest wages.

US-NJ.reading: A flat 85% of the average weekly wage.

US-NY.reading: A flat 67% of the average weekly wage.

US-OR.reading: Not read: the pages fetched give a sliding scale without its percentages.

US-RI.reading: Not read: the program's pages refuse the container.

US-VA.reading: Up to 80% of the average weekly wage.

US-WA.reading: Up to 90% of weekly pay; the 90% goes to lower wages.
